title: Bidirectional Dijkstra Finds Routes Faster in Reykjavík
description: Watch how Bidirectional Dijkstra searches from both the start and goal at the same time to meet in the middle. This dramatically reduces explored street segments on a real-world style grid graph.
ig_caption:
🧭✨ Reykjavík streets, but make it math: Bidirectional Dijkstra works by running two Dijkstra frontiers—one forward from the start node and one backward from the destination—until they converge.

🔍 Graph theory time: we model the street network as a weighted graph (nodes = intersections, edges = road segments with costs like distance/time). Unlike plain Dijkstra that expands outward from a single source, Bidirectional Dijkstra alternates expansions and stops when the best combined path is guaranteed, which can cut down the explored area dramatically on large maps.

🌍 In this visualization, each “wave” is a priority-queue expansion driven by smallest tentative distance—so the meeting point becomes the key to reconstructing the optimal route.

yt_description:
Bidirectional Dijkstra visualization in Reykjavík (Laugardalur)! 🚦 This video explains how running two synchronized Dijkstra searches (forward from start, backward from goal) can meet in the middle and speed up optimal shortest-path finding. 

#shorts-friendly mechanics: weighted graph model, priority queue expansions, early stopping when the optimal combined distance is provably found, then path reconstruction.
